text: Seán William "Jack" McLoughlin (/məˈɡlɒklɪn/ mə-GLOK-lin; born 7 February 1990), known online as jacksepticeye, is an Irish YouTuber whose content centers on gaming, comedy, and vlogging. Born the youngest of five children to John (c. 1936 – 27 January 2021) and Florrie McLoughlin, he was raised in Cloghan, County Offaly, Ireland, and also lived in Banagher. His father worked for the Electricity Supply Board and his mother worked various jobs before becoming a caregiver for his grandmother. McLoughlin began playing video games at age seven, often spending time in a treehouse with a Nintendo Game Boy, where he found a sense of belonging. He was commonly called Jack in childhood and received the nickname "Jack Septic Eye" after injuring his eye during a football match. At 18, he and his family moved to a cabin in Ballycumber, where he studied music technology and production at Limerick Institute of Technology before dropping out to return home. He later moved to Athlone, County Westmeath, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) degree in hotel management from the Athlone Institute of Technology. In 2017, he moved to Brighton, England, partly due to privacy concerns after fans discovered his home in Athlone and to access the city’s strong LGBTQ and vegan communities. He began uploading videos to YouTube under the name "jacksepticeye" in December 2012, initially focusing on voice impressions before shifting to gameplay content. His channel gained rapid traction, reaching 15,000 subscribers in four days after being mentioned in a PewDiePie video, hitting one million subscribers in August 2014, 1.5 million by year-end, one billion views and 3.2 million subscribers by February 2015, and adding six million subscribers the following year. In January 2016, he was one of the first YouTubers signed under PewDiePie’s Revelmode network, co-hosted the SXSW Gaming Awards, and appeared in the 2016 YouTube Rewind. The Revelmode network was shut down by Disney in 2017 due to controversy over anti-semitic imagery in a planned Scare PewDiePie season, after which McLoughlin was signed to Disney’s Digital Network. In June 2017, he was featured in Polaris: Player Select on Disney XD as part of the D | XP programming block and was included in RTÉ 2’s Ireland's Rich List as one of the "top 30 earners under 30." He toured the US and UK in 2017 and 2018 with his How Did We Get Here tour and the Game Grumps' Ready Player 3 tour, with the show featuring a biographical retelling of his life and fan gameplay segments. In February 2018, he announced US and Canada dates for the tour, performing at the Just for Laughs comedy festival in Montreal in July 2018. In 2018, he began streaming exclusive content on Twitch under a multi-year deal with Disney Digital Network. In January 2019, he signed with WME and later joined Studio71. In 2020, he participated in Summer Game Fest following the cancellation of E3. He appeared in the film Free Guy starring Ryan Reynolds, which was released in August 2021, and previously played Deadpool with Reynolds in a video. He also advised director Shawn Levy on making the film authentic to video game culture. In July 2021, he released a short film titled "15 MONTHS" about his pandemic experience, and later signed with CAA. In February 2022, a biographical documentary entitled How Did We Get Here? premiered on Moment House, featuring footage from his tour. In July 2022, he stated he would likely stop streaming on Twitch to focus on edited YouTube content. In 2023, he co-hosted The Gamer and the Mouth with Chris Redd. In 2025, he voiced the character 'Punch Up' in the video game Dispatch, starring Aaron Paul. He has also worked on production and behind-the-scenes roles for a cancelled animated show based on Soma and an independent horror film called Godmother. McLoughlin has been recognized in numerous media lists, including Forbes' Top Gaming Influencers 2017, as the eighth highest-paid YouTuber in 2018 (estimated $16 million), eighth highest-paid gamer in 2019 ($11 million), and third most talked-about gaming personality on Twitter. He was featured in the 2020 Forbes 30 Under 30 list under "Sports & Games" as Ireland's most popular YouTuber. In 2021, he was the sixth most popular gaming streamer according to Currys, and ranked 15th in Forbes' Top Creators 2022 and 2023, with estimated incomes of €7.3 million (2022) and $27 million (2023), and $18 million in 2024. His channel has consistently been noted as the most subscribed in Ireland by publications such as Tubefilter, The Irish Examiner, The Irish Times, The Times, and The Guardian. His content primarily consists of Let's Plays, comedy gaming videos, and vlogs, featuring a mix of conventional and unusual games, collaborations with Markiplier and PewDiePie, interviews with celebrities like Tom Holland, Dwayne Johnson, Brad Pitt, Chris Hemsworth, and Margot Robbie, and regular appearances of comedy sketches, charity livestreams, and Q&A sessions. Videos typically begin with a high five and the catchphrase "Top of the morning to ya, laddies," though he used it less by 2023, and end with "punch the 'like' button in the face, like a boss!" The color green, representing his Irish heritage, appears in his YouTube logo "Septic Eye Sam." His commentary is improvised, humorous, and includes swearing, described as "genuine" and "authentic," and he calls himself the "most energetic video-game commentator on YouTube," noting his content is an "assault on the senses" that people either love or hate. He attributes his success to energy, positivity, honesty, and consistency and emphasizes building an inclusive community, promoting the slogan "positive mental attitude." Elements of gothic storytelling appear in his horror game Let's Plays and in the character Antisepticeye, which originated in response to Markiplier’s Darkiplier and involves direct audience interaction on social media. His audience creates fan fiction, and he produces short-form videos for TikTok focusing on personal content. For the first five years, he uploaded two videos per day, later reducing to one per day. In July 2018, he announced a break due to mental health and burnout, a trend he repeated in July 2020 and January 2021 (after his father’s death) and again in July 2021, stating he needed to step back to avoid burnout. In October 2018, he co-founded the clothing brand Cloak with Markiplier, which later added Pokimane as a partner and created special editions with franchises like Minecraft Dungeons and Five Nights at Freddy's, donating a percentage of sales to charities such as the World Health Organization and The Trevor Project; he left the brand in 2023. On 15 June 2020, he launched Top of The Mornin' Coffee, partnering with the Feya Foundation to combat world hunger. In April 2023, he launched a podcast with Ethan Nestor titled Brain Leak and announced a comic book with Bad Egg.

Twitch streamer Pokimane serves as a third partner and creative director for the brand, which has launched special edition collections in collaboration with franchises and internet personalities such as Minecraft Dungeons, Five Nights at Freddy's, Rhett & Link, and Pokimane. The brand donates a percentage of its sales revenue to charities, having contributed to the World Health Organization's COVID-19 Solidarity Response Fund and The Trevor Project. On 15 June 2020, McLoughlin announced the launch of his coffee company, Top of The Mornin' Coffee, which began pre-orders on that day, and partnered with the Feya Foundation to combat world hunger. In April 2023, he launched a podcast with YouTuber Ethan Nestor titled Brain Leak. He also announced a comic book with publisher Bad Egg, inspired by their collaboration with MoistCr1TiKaL on Godslap; the series, Altrverse, features characters from his YouTube content and had its first issue released in December 2023. Business Insider has labeled McLoughlin "one of YouTube's most prolific philanthropists." In 2019, he received a Humanitarian Stream Team award from Save the Children for fundraising efforts. In 2021, he was named one of Junior Chamber International Ireland's "Ten Outstanding Young Persons" for raising over $6 million in charity between 2017 and 2021. In 2022, he won Best Philanthropic Streamer at The Streamer Awards. In December 2016, McLoughlin participated in the Revelmode charity livestream #Cringemas with PewDiePie, Markiplier, Emma Blackery, and PJ Liguori, raising over $1.3 million under the #EndAIDS hashtag with matching donations from the Gates Foundation and YouTube. In December 2017, he hosted two charity streams with Blackery and Liguori for Save The Children, raising over $260,000. Throughout 2018, he hosted multiple fundraiser livestreams for charities including the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, the Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance, GameChanger, AbleGamers, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, and Crisis Text Line, raising over $1 million that year; his Crisis Text Line stream in December was titled "Thankmas," a name he later used annually. In January 2019, he raised over $100,000 for the Make-A-Wish Foundation. In March 2019, he headlined a Charity: Water livestream, raising over $100,000. In May 2019, he raised over $110,000 in nine hours for Red Nose Day 2019. In September 2019, he hosted a stream with actor Emilia Clarke, raising $260,000 for SameYou, a charity focused on brain injury recovery. In December 2019, he raised over $300,000 for Child's Play during his annual Thankmas stream. In January 2020, he raised over $200,000 in four hours for Australian bushfires. In April 2020, he raised over $650,000 in 12 hours for COVID-19 relief, with the #HopeFromHome campaign raising over $1.7 million in total through subsequent streams. In June 2020, he raised over $600,000 for Black Lives Matter organizations including The Bail Project, NAACP Empowerment Programs, Color of Change, and the Advancement Project. In October 2020, he participated in MrBeast's Team Trees campaign, raising over $150,000 for the Arbor Day Foundation. In December 2020, his Thankmas stream raised over $1.4 million in 10 hours for Red Nose Day, with the campaign raising over $4.6 million in total. In December 2021, he partnered with Tiltify for a Thankmas stream supporting New Story, which combats homelessness through 3D-printed houses; Tiltify enabled influencers to host additional streams, and the campaign raised $7.6 million. In November 2022, he announced a new partnership with Tiltify to raise $10 million for World Central Kitchen during his annual Thankmas stream, a goal that was successfully met in the final hour. His 2023 Thankmas stream, presented live from the Orpheum Theater in Los Angeles, raised $6 million for World Central Kitchen, bringing the total from his Thankmas streams to over $25 million. His 2024 Thankmas stream was also broadcast live from the Orpheum Theater in support of Crisis Text Line. McLoughlin has criticized YouTube's changing algorithms and policies, stating in November 2016 that removing ads from "unsuitable content" was a "shitty thing to do" and accusing the platform of using "shady tactics" and "manipulating viewers" after algorithm changes reduced views and subscribers. In May 2018, he objected to a surprise algorithm test that altered video order in subscription feeds, urging YouTube to keep such changes on the home page and recommendations. In March 2022, he released a video criticizing increased scams and spam comments on his videos, a concern echoed by Linus Sebastian and Marques Brownlee, leading YouTube to implement new policies that removed the ability for channels to hide subscriber counts or use special characters in channel names to prevent impersonation and expanded enhanced comment moderation access. McLoughlin has criticized the YouTube algorithm for pressuring creators to constantly produce content and has discussed creator mental health, suggesting the platform could hide view counts or remove the dislike button, while also noting that YouTube provided him with "purpose" and reduced his loneliness and depression. He believes YouTube's strength lies in its sense of community, stating that people seek community wherever they can. He has positively reviewed YouTube Gaming following policy changes at Twitch that reduced revenue shares, saying "What a mess. Owned by Amazon and acting like some amateur platform. It's no wonder so many of your partners are jumping ship to YT." In 2023, McLoughlin claimed MrBeast had damaged YouTube by making it more focused on views, money, and popularity than fun; MrBeast initially called the comments "insanely disrespectful" but later stated they had a private conversation and there was no animosity. McLoughlin believes video game culture should be more inclusive, criticizing controversies involving companies like Activision Blizzard and the use of slurs or "gamer words" on Twitch as evidence of toxic "chad energy," and stating that a more accepting, open culture is needed, similar to progress in real life and LGBTQ representation. He dated Danish influencer Signe "Wiishu" Hansen from 2015 to 2018 and has been in a relationship with Dutch YouTuber Evelien "Gab" Smolders since 2019. McLoughlin has played the drums since childhood and became a fan of heavy metal music through his older brother. He was formerly in a melodic death metal-influenced metalcore band called Raised to the Ground. He has autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
